newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares waver, recovery seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares waver, recovery seen soon.

text.p: Singapore shares wavered in early trade on Thursday, but dealers predicted an upturn once the corporate reporting season ends.
"We're getting near to the final stages of the fall and the market has got to go up from there," a local dealer said.
"There's another week before the season ends and the market gets back on track. I'm confident the bounce will come, it's just a matter of when," said another.
At 0250 GMT, the barometer Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was down 3.41 at 2,117.15, with selected selling of blue chip index stocks early trading's main feature.
"Blue chip earnings aren't that great so it doesn't help the STII," one dealer said.
Early volume was a slim 40.2 million shares producing 97 gainers and 90 losers.
Great Eastern Life led early losers, down Singapore $0.80 at S$22.40 on tiny volume, with FJ Benjamin shares down S$0.185 at S$0.955 on more substantive volume of 2.3 million units.

Early gainers were topped by Samanda Holdings, up S$0.70 at S$7.80 with over-the-counter-traded Palmco Holdings up S$0.13 to S$2.36 after its Kuala Lumpur listing was suspended pending an announcement.
